To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) impersonal presentational constructions are more likely to occur in thetic-XV than in thetic-V1 environments, and that (ii) impersonal presentations tend to occur with expletives that attract subject properties.
impersonal presentational constructions are typically associated with thetic-XV and that personal presentational constructions are associated with thetic-V1.
thetic-V1 and thetic-XV are two parameters of a language-level typology of presentational constructions, and that thetic-V 1 is negatively correlated with impersonality.

the following questions: What are the properties of the subject in presentational constructions in Germanic and Romance?
the distribution of impersonality in presentational constructions, with the aim to contribute towards a more general understanding of the phenomenon of impersonality in the grammar.
the distribution of impersonal vs. personal presentational constructions across languages and language types.

in thetic sentences, there is a correlation between the parameters ‘type of exple-tive’ (impersonal vs. personal) and ‘type of existential predi-cate’ (impersonally used existential verb vs. impersonally used expletive) on the one hand and the parameter ‘thetic-XV vs. thetic-V1’ on the other.

the distribution of subject property attraction in presentational constructions is a matter of language-level typology.
